history.summary: CSV STATE FLAG: the CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name; the temple is in Akola, MAHARASHTRA (CSV town 'Akola' is correct). Known locally as Birla Ram Mandir or Shri Ram Mandir, this is a modern Hindu temple and the private shrine of the Birla family, built by M/s Berar Oil Industries of the Birla family (per local reviews and rkvsmakola.in). It stands in Tapadia Nagar/Jathar Peth along the railway line at Oak Marg, Akola. The main shrine houses Bhagavan Ram with Devi Sita and Lakshman, with a separate Bhagavan Shiva shrine beside it; all idols are pure white marble. The walls carry Gita verses and famous hymns/mantras selected from the Vedas and Upanishads with small paintings and photos. Local devotees describe it as an old, calm, less-crowded temple; an annual Ramnavami yatra is held. No source gives a construction date or detailed founding history (flag as unverified). One travel site (peopleplaces.in) describes this entry with Delhi Birla Mandir facts - that conflation is ignored here.
